rationale: The four-view diagram is coherent as one object and the parcel containment is acceptable, so repair integrity is high. However, for neighborhood living the mass reads as a compact, almost decorative cross/rosette object with a weakly legible street threshold. The verified access edge is not answered by a strong public void, seam, canopy, or undercut; the notch is too small to read as an active entry condition. In section, the object remains mostly boxy with a stepped/creased top rather than a program-bearing roof or inhabited ground figure. It is therefore not program-fit despite having a stable silhouette in all views. The form also does not resonate strongly with the most relevant references, which emphasize public ground response, courtyard/void logic, or clear base-plus-upper hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More open and site-responsive than the candidate; candidate lacks comparable public void and reads more compact/closed.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise, horizontally spread mass with a clearly legible central void/courtyard and a public-facing ground condition.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is much flatter and more pavilion-like; candidate’s polygonal crown is not supported by an equivalent ground threshold.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple pavilion-like massing with a clear entry setback and canopy condition at the ground edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate is less articulated at the street edge and relies on a single compact object rather than a clear base/support relationship.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Attached streetwall with offset volumes and a readable hierarchy between base and upper mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual only; candidate does not have the same section-driven publicness or terrace logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/courtyard section can produce strong inhabited voids when the section is the primary spatial idea.

warnings: Visible massing is coherent across views but semantically under-addresses the access edge.
The current notch is too minor to count as a meaningful public threshold.
The silhouette is more sculptural than capacity- or program-driven for neighborhood living.
